report.incidentSummary: On 2026-10-16 starting around 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC), auth-service OTP login verification success rate dropped precipitously from ~97.4% to ~70%, accompanied by an elevated OTP send retry volume peaking at 1285/min. Internal notification and queue pipelines operated normally without backpressure, and shared cache metrics showed no memory or eviction anomalies. The drop is consistent with downstream telecom operator delivery latency or routing degradation under the external SMS provider, causing OTP codes to arrive after their expiration window as seen in past incident PIR-1602.
report.rootCauseStatement: Downstream external telecom carrier delivery latency or routing degradation via the SMS provider delayed the delivery of OTP SMS messages beyond their client-side validity window, resulting in users submitting expired OTPs and experiencing failed login attempts despite normal internal HTTP dispatch acceptance.

hypotheses.cause: External SMS provider routing degradation or downstream telecom operator delivery delay causing OTP messages to arrive late, leading users to submit expired codes.
hypotheses.rationale: Internal delivery queues and notification dispatch functioned without backpressure or API errors (308 successful handoffs to sms-provider, steady ~120ms latency, ~2s queue lag, no sms_send_failures spike). auth-service OTP success rate plunged directly at 05:10 UTC with a retry surge, precisely matching historical incident PIR-1602 where carrier delivery latency caused OTPs to arrive after TTL expiration.

hypotheses.cause: Host disruption, pod restart, or clock skew induced by the log shipper upgrade (CHG-48221) on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48221 was completed at 04:54 UTC, but auth-service OTP success rate remained normal (~97.4%) until 05:10 UTC (a 16-minute gap). Furthermore, auth-service latency p95 remained rock-steady (~280-315ms) and error rate remained at baseline until 05:10 UTC with zero system warnings or errors.

facts.statement: auth-service otp_success_rate fell sharply from ~97.4% at 05:05 UTC to 87.04% at 05:10 UTC, settling between 68% and 72% thereafter.
auth-service otp_sent_per_min surged from ~980-1010/min baseline to 1076/min at 05:10 UTC, peaking at 1285/min at 05:25 UTC.
notification-service latency_p95_ms remained stable between 110.8 ms and 126.2 ms, and sms_send_failures remained flat at baseline (~3/min) across the entire window.
message-queue consumer_lag_s on the notifications queue was flat at ~2.08 seconds with normal queue depth (~110 messages).
notification-service logged 308 successful SMS handoffs to sms-provider for OTPs without HTTP API rejections.
Shared cache memory utilization remained stable at ~62%, evictions stayed between 31 and 42/min, and sessions cache hit rate stayed at ~95%.
CHG-48221 upgraded the log shipper agent on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC, after which auth-service log shipping stopped at 04:54:07 UTC.
auth-service latency_p95_ms remained stable at ~297 ms across the window, showing no performance degradation after 04:54 UTC or 05:10 UTC.

inferences.statement: The surge in OTP dispatches between 05:10 and 05:25 UTC is driven by end users retrying OTP requests when the SMS fails to arrive promptly.
Because notification-service and message-queue telemetry indicate flawless internal dispatch, message delivery delays are occurring external to our infrastructure at the SMS gateway or carrier level.

The log shipper upgrade (CHG-48221) at 04:54 UTC broke log forwarding from auth-service containers but did not cause the verification failure, as request latencies were unaffected and the failure onset did not occur until 05:10 UTC.

assumptions.statement: OTP codes have a short validity window (typically 3-5 minutes), making them sensitive to operator-side transit delays.
Downstream telecom carriers accepted SMS payloads via the aggregator API but experienced queueing or throttling in specific telecom circles.

timeline.event: CHG-48221 completed: log shipper agent upgraded on auth-service node pool; auth-service log collection ceased at 04:54:07 UTC.
auth-service OTP verification success rate remains normal at 97.44%.
Incident onset: OTP success rate drops sharply to 87.04% and error_rate begins rising to 2.16%; OTP send requests jump to 1076/min.
OTP success rate plunges to 71.99%; OTP sends increase to 1243/min due to user retries.
OTP send rate peaks at 1285/min; success rate hovers around 69.92%.
On-call SRE raises SEV1 incident INC-6097 noting OTP login success drop.

confidence.rationale: Internal systems (cache, notification-service, message-queue, api-gateway) show completely healthy execution and baseline metrics, and auth-service request latency is steady. The drop precisely mirrors past incident PIR-1602. Direct downstream telecom delivery receipts (DLRs) could not be queried directly from internal telemetry, preventing higher confidence.

gaps.description: auth-service stopped emitting logs after CHG-48221 at 04:54:07 UTC, preventing inspection of granular OTP failure error codes (e.g., OTP_EXPIRED).
gaps.impact: Verification failure causes could not be observed directly in auth-service application logs.

gaps.description: Carrier delivery receipts (DLR) and delivery receipt latency metrics are not exported by the internal telemetry store or notification-service.
gaps.impact: External operator-side transit delays cannot be verified via internal time series metrics.

recommendedActions.action: Trigger failover of OTP SMS traffic to the secondary SMS provider route or fallback provider.
recommendedActions.rationale: PIR-2004 and PIR-1602 demonstrated that routing around degraded SMS carrier routes immediately recovers OTP verification completion rates.
recommendedActions.verification: Monitor auth-service otp_success_rate returning to >97% and otp_sent_per_min returning to ~1000/min baseline.

recommendedActions.action: Fix log shipper configuration on auth-service node pool to restore log ingestion.
recommendedActions.rationale: CHG-48221 halted auth-service log streaming at 04:54:07 UTC, blinding on-call engineers to application-level exceptions and verification logs.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify that query_logs for auth-service begins returning active logs with current timestamps.

recommendedActions.action: Implement delivery receipt latency (DLR) metrics and automated provider failover thresholds in notification-service.
recommendedActions.rationale: Delivery latency degradation at downstream telecom operators is invisible to HTTP-level send metrics and causes silent user-facing authentication failures.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm notification-service publishes delivery_receipt_latency_s and triggers automated alerts or rerouting.
